A Long Guide to Local-First Tools

Section one introduces the idea of local-first software and why it matters for privacy.

Chapter 1: Principles

Local-first tools keep the primary copy of data on the user device instead of a remote server.

They continue to work offline and never require an account to perform their core function.

Chapter 2: Storage

Files are written directly to the local disk using standard download mechanisms.

Formats such as PDF and Markdown are portable and readable across every platform.

Chapter 3: Capture

Visual capture walks the page from top to bottom, one viewport at a time.

Each captured segment becomes one page of the final document.

Chapter 4: Extraction

Text extraction prefers semantic containers such as article and main elements.

When no semantic container exists, density analysis finds the richest text block.

Chapter 5: Limits

Very long pages are truncated at a safe height to avoid exhausting browser memory.

Infinite scrolling feeds can never be fully captured, and that is documented clearly.

Chapter 6: Conclusion

Keeping both a visual copy and a text copy gives users the best of both worlds.

The final paragraph closes the guide with a reminder that all processing stays local.
